problems.statement_en: S = {a 1 , a 2 , ... , a n , b 1 , b 2 , ... , b n }. There are subsets C 1 , C 2 , ... , C k , such that (1) for no i, j do both a i and b i both belong to C j , (2) for any pair of distinct elements of S, not of the form a i , b i , there is just one C j containing both elements. Show that if n > 3, then k ≥ 2n. (USA 3) -->

problems.statement_en: Find the number of ways of partitioning {1, 2, 3, ... , n} into three (possibly empty) subsets A, B, C such that (1) for each subset, if the elements are written in ascending order, then they alternate in parity, and (2) if all three subsets are non-empty, then just one of them has its smallest element even. (Poland 1) -->
